scenario: AITA for calling the police on my daughter to teach her a lesson about stealing? | My daughter is in the sixth grade. Every morning, I have her take a couple of dollars out of my wallet for lunch money. In the last few weeks, several times I have noticed that I am missing a little bit more money than usual. So, this week, I planted a 20 dollar bill before my daughter took her lunch money out. Sure enough, she took it. I called the police and asked them to come with me to the school so that we could teach my daughter a lesson. Two officers met me there and we pulled my daughter out of class, after which she informed one of the officers that there has been a bully who is stealing her lunch money/forcing my daughter to buy her lunch. She also has been buying lunch for one of her friends who can not afford it. This was confirmed by both the bully, and the friend. My daughter was silent on the way home and i informed her that I was just trying to teach her a lesson, that stealing is wrong and can get you in a lot of trouble. and that in the future she needs to speak to myself or her mother if there are issues at school and we would be happy to help her resolve them. When we got home, my wife absolutely lost her shit on me, in full tears, telling me that this is a one way ticket to estrangement from our daughter in the future and that we should have just asked her why she was stealing money. She would have just lied about stealing in the first place so I really don’t understand what her idea of a solution is. My daughter apparently told my wife that she is terrified that her bully will now retaliate, and also that she may have lost her friend for bringing so much attention to her financial issue. She apologized for stealing and said she just didn’t want us to intervene. I am wondering if I really did the wrong thing here. AITA?

My daughter is in sixth grade, and every morning I give her a couple of dollars for lunch money. Over the last few weeks, I noticed that I was missing a bit more money than usual. So, this week, I planted a $20 bill before she took her lunch money. Sure enough, she took it. I called the police and asked them to come with me to the school to teach her a lesson about stealing. When we got to the school, the officers pulled her out of class. She then told one of the officers that there had been a bully who was stealing her lunch money and forcing her to buy lunch for the bully. She also mentioned that she had been buying lunch for one of her friends who couldn't afford it. Both the bully and the friend confirmed this. My daughter was silent on the way home, and I told her that I was just trying to teach her a lesson, that stealing is wrong and can get her into a lot of trouble, and that in the future she should talk to me or her mother if there are issues at school and we would be happy to help her resolve them. When we got home, my wife absolutely lost it, in full tears, telling me that this was a one-way ticket to estrangement from our daughter in the future and that we should have just asked her why she was stealing money. She said that my daughter would have just lied about stealing in the first place, so I really don't understand what her idea of a solution is. My daughter apparently told my wife that she is terrified that her bully will now retaliate, and also that she may have lost her friend for bringing so much attention to her financial issue. She apologized for stealing and said she just didn't want us to intervene. I'm wondering if I really did the wrong thing here. AITA? (Am I the Asshole?) Alright, so first, I need to understand the dynamics here. My daughter was taking extra money, which I assumed was stealing. But it turned out she was using the money to buy lunch for herself because a bully was stealing her lunch money and forcing her to buy lunch for the bully. She was also helping a friend who couldn't afford lunch. So, she was taking extra money to cover these expenses. I called the police to teach her a lesson about stealing, but in reality, she was taking the money to deal with a difficult situation at school involving a bully and a friend in need. When the police came, she revealed this information, and it was confirmed by both the bully and the friend. After the incident, my daughter was silent on the way home, and I tried to explain to her that stealing is wrong and that she should talk to us if there are issues at school. However, my wife was furious, saying that this approach would damage our relationship with our daughter and that we should have handled it differently by talking to her first. My daughter also expressed fear that the bully would retaliate and that she might lose her friend because of the attention brought to her financial situation. She apologized for stealing and said she didn't want us to intervene. So, the question is: Was calling the police on my daughter the right thing to do? Did I act appropriately, or did I overreact? To answer this, I need to consider several factors: 1. **Understanding the Situation**: Did I fully understand why my daughter was taking extra money before deciding to call the police? It seems like I assumed she was stealing without considering other possibilities. 2. **Teaching the Lesson**: Was calling the police an appropriate way to teach her about the consequences of stealing? Or was there a better way to address the issue? 3. **Impact on Relationships**: How did this action affect my relationship with my daughter and my wife's relationship with her? My wife was upset, and my daughter seemed scared and upset. 4. **Alternative Approaches**: What could I have done differently to address the issue without involving the police? 5. **Long-term Consequences**: What are the potential long-term effects of this action on my daughter's behavior and our family dynamics? 6. **Moral and Ethical Considerations**: Is it morally justifiable to call the police on a child for stealing when the stealing was done to address other issues? 7. **Legal Implications**: Are there legal implications for calling the police on a minor for such an offense? 8. **School's Role**: Should the school have been involved in addressing the bullying and financial issues instead of the police? 9. **Support for My Daughter**: Did my daughter receive the support she needed to deal with the bully and her friend's financial situation? 10. **Communication**: How could communication have been improved between me, my wife, and my daughter to prevent this situation? Considering these factors, it seems like there might have been a better way to handle the situation without involving the police. Perhaps talking to my daughter first to understand why she was taking extra money, addressing the bullying issue with the school, and finding a way to support her friend financially would have been more effective. Involving the police might have been seen as an overreaction, especially since the stealing was done to address other problems. It could have caused unnecessary stress and fear for my daughter, potentially damaging our relationship. Additionally, my wife's reaction indicates that she felt this approach was harmful to our family dynamics, which is an important consideration. Overall, while I intended to teach my daughter a lesson about stealing, the way I went about it might have been more harmful than helpful, and there could have been alternative approaches to address the underlying issues more effectively.
